title: What If US Treasuries Rebound?
text:
What If US Treasuries Rebound?

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 5 Oct 2026

One of the more bewildering developments of the quarter-end was the complete lack of a rebound in long-dated US treasuries. After all, with equities posting a decent quarter, and bonds being taken to the woodshed, one might have imagined some kind of quarter-end rebalancing by large pension funds, insurance companies, or even RIAs selling equities to buy bonds. The weakness in US non-farm payrolls, the disappointing growth in China (see Governance Over Growth), the gathering clouds over France (see Falling OATs And A Divided France)… all would have also pointed towards US government bonds catching a bid. This did not happen.Instead, as last week ended, the 14-day RSI on the long-dated bond ETF hit 14.9; a sign, if ever there was one, of the little regard in which long-dated US treasuries are currently held. This is understandable: it has been an ugly quarter, year, three years, five years, and decade for long- dated bonds. A dismal performance in which many important political, geopolitical, and economic shifts have played a hand: runaway budget deficits, wars, weaponization of the US dollar and of the US treasury market, protectionism… The bearish case for US treasuries is, at this stage, obvious enough.
